'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Battle of Khartoum (2023–2025)|Battle of Khartoum]]
***[[Germany]] announces the suspension of its attempt to rescue 150 German citizens from [[Khartoum]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2023/04/19/world/africa/japan-evacuations-sudan.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/germany-forced-halt-evacuation-mission-sudan-spiegel-2023-04-19/ (Reuters)]
**[[Sudanese refugee crisis]]
***Thousands of Sudanese [[civilian]]s cross the closed [[Chad–Sudan border|border]] with [[Chad]] as [[refugee]]s and are [[immigration detention|detained]], according to Chadian Defence Minister Daoud Yaya Brahim. Brahim also states that the [[Chad National Army]] detained and disarmed a contingent of 320 [[Sudanese troops]] who crossed the border. [https://www.trtworld.com/africa/hundreds-of-sudanese-troops-flee-to-chad-as-fighting-rages-67223 (TRT World)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/chad-disarmed-sudanese-contingent-which-entered-its-territory-monday-defence-2023-04-19/ (Reuters)] 
**[[Evacuation of foreign nationals during the Sudanese civil war]]
***The [[United Kingdom]], [[Germany]], and [[Japan]] urge their citizens to seek shelter, hide, or [[emergency evacuation|evacuate]] due to ongoing fighting. [https://news.sky.com/story/sudan-ceasefire-in-tatters-as-fighting-continues-around-khartoum-12861042 (Sky News)] [https://theprint.in/world/germany-forced-to-halt-evacuation-mission-from-sudan-spiegel/1527675/ (The Print India)]
***[[Japan]][[Japanese people|ese]] [[Chief Cabinet Secretary]] [[Hirokazu Matsuno]] says that Japan will send a [[Japanese Self-Defense Forces|Self-Defense Forces]] aircraft to evacuate 60 Japanese nationals from [[Sudan]]. [https://www.asahi.com/sp/ajw/articles/14889095 (''Asahi Shimbun'')]
**Satellite imagery reveals that at least one [[Egyptian Air Force]] [[Mikoyan MiG-29|MiG-29]] was destroyed at an [[airbase]] in [[Merowe, Sudan|Merowe]], with at least two others heavily damaged. [https://www.thedrive.com/the-war-zone/egyptian-mig-29s-destroyed-in-sudan (The Drive)]
*[[Mali War]]
**Four people are killed and several others are reported missing after [[jihadism|jihadists]] [[ambush]] a [[Politics of Mali|Malian government]] [[delegation]] near [[Nara, Mali|Nara]], [[Koulikoro Region]], [[Mali]]. [https://www.barrons.com/news/four-dead-in-attack-on-mali-govt-convoy-officials-4c28b4f4 (''Barron's'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2023 Canadian federal worker strike]]
**Over 155,000 [[Canada|Canadian]] federal workers go on [[strike action|strike]] after the [[Public Service Alliance of Canada]] failed to reach an agreement with the [[government of Canada|government]] over pay raises and [[remote work]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-65325863 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Sanaa crowd crush]]
**At least 90 people are killed and 322 others are injured in a [[crowd crush]] in [[Sanaa]], [[Yemen]] during a charity event. [https://egyptindependent.com/90-people-killed-more-than-300-injured-in-sanaa-stampede (Egypt Independent)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[List of heat waves#2023|List of heat waves]]
**A heatwave in Asia leads to deaths and school closures in [[India]], and record-breaking temperatures in other countries. [[Luang Prabang]], [[Laos]], recorded a temperature of {{convert|42.7|C}}, while [[Tak province|Tak]], [[Thailand]], recorded a temperature of {{convert|44.6|C}}. [https://www.theguardian.com/weather/2023/apr/19/severe-heatwave-asia-deaths-schools-close-india-china (''The Guardian'')]
*A report by the [[United Nations Population Fund]] estimates that [[India]] will surpass [[China]] as [[List of countries and dependencies by population|the most populous country in the world]] by the middle of this year. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/india-overtakes-china-worlds-most-populous-country-rcna80364 (NBC News)]
 
'''International relations'''
*[[Bulgaria–Ukraine relations]]
**[[Bulgaria]] temporarily bans the import of grain from [[Ukraine]], except for those in transit, following similar decisions made by [[Poland]], [[Hungary]], and [[Slovakia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/ukraine-crisis-grains-bulgaria-idAFL8N36M2G7 (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Crime in Costa Rica]]
**President [[Rodrigo Chaves]] orders a series of measures to fight increasing crime in [[Costa Rica]], including the deployment of more police, tougher juvenile laws, extradition of foreign criminals, and restrictions on the sale of ammunition. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/costa-rica-president-gets-tougher-security-crime-soars-2023-04-19/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[8 January Brasília attacks|2023 Brazilian Congress attack]]
**[[Institutional Security Bureau|Secretary of Institutional Security]] of [[Brazil]] [[Marco Edson Gonçalves Dias]] resigns over his presence at the [[Palácio do Planalto|presidential palace]] during the attack. He is replaced by [[Ricardo Cappelli]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/top-security-adviser-brazils-president-abruptly-resigns-2023-04-19/ (Reuters)]
